AN EMERGENT WORLD RESEARCH PROGRAM

From first rules
to possible worlds.

What if chemistry, life, technology, and society could unfold from one continuous simulated history?

SimWorld is exploring that question, starting with a reproducible physical seed and a transparent roadmap for everything that follows.

01 / THE RESEARCH

One history.
Many levels of explanation.

The ambition is a world whose higher-level patterns follow from interactions. The method is to build and validate each connection, one experiment at a time.

A

What exists today

A Python model of a hot seed that expands, cools, forms effective nuclei, and captures electrons. Event logs and state hashes make its history reproducible within the tested environment.

Inspect the evidence ↗
B

What comes next

A hierarchy of proposed models: atomic structure, chemistry, materials, planets, life, learning, technology, and institutions. Every layer needs its own validation and error budget.

Follow the roadmap ↗
C

What counts as progress

Repeatable experiments, independently checked results, and clear limits. A plausible world is a starting point; a defensible model explains what its rules can and cannot establish.

03 / EVIDENCE AND LIMITS

Reproducible is a beginning.
Validation is the next step.

A fresh run reproduced the archived summary, event log, and all 34 state hashes. The same audit identified important gaps that passing tests alone did not reveal.

OPEN SCIENTIFIC QUESTIONS

Do reverse reactions reach equilibrium?

The audit found nuclear reverse pathways absent in some product-only states, and fully neutral atomic states that cannot photoionize. Equilibrium needs tests from both directions.

Are stochastic draws independent?

Some calls reuse random-stream prefixes. Exact replay is demonstrated, but reproducibility does not establish statistical independence.

Does the performance prototype describe this engine?

The array-storage microbenchmark and the current dictionary-based engine use different representations. Prototype throughput is not an end-to-end performance result.

Have life or civilizations emerged?

No. Those systems are proposed research. The baseline is an effective stochastic physical model, not a first-principles derivation of a complete universe.

REPRODUCE THE BASELINE

A history you can run again.

Use Python 3.11.9 with the pinned dependencies in the source package. The audit used NumPy 2.4.6 and pytest 9.1.1.

TERMINAL · FROM THE SOURCE FOLDER
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python -m sim.demo --seed 42 --ticks 3400 --cells 8 --probe-cells 2,3 --out reproduced_m4
python -m sim.replay reproduced_m4
